test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 16 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). C is sitting second to the left of A. Only one person is sitting between B and C when counted from right of B. E is sitting third to the right of F. D is sitting to the immediate left of E. The position of how many persons excluding A will remain unchanged if all the persons are arranged in the English alphabetical order in clockwise direction, starting from A, keeping the position of A unchanged?
solution:
Given:

Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre.

C is sitting second to the left of A. Only one person is sitting between B and C when counted from right of B.

E is sitting third to the right of F.

D is sitting to the immediate left of E.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/790da5b89049ebade70e4dbbc9265a5a6fdd79085f2b3228a915f55254f9826d.png] 

Now, position of persons excluding A will remain unchanged if all the persons are arranged in the English alphabetical order in clockwise direction, starting from A

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a85ba2d3f64f2332ec40c2d2b432b24c2c9502d98b91dce3d78587e1a87195f7.png] 

Thus, only 'C' will remain unchanged.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**
